aspects.says: Reading a serialized singleton builds a new object without running its constructor, so the constructor guard never sees it, and the copy carries the state it was written with.
basis: section:Deserialization Makes a Second Instance Without Running the Constructor

aspects.says: An enum constant is a static field like any other, so an enum singleton is also one per class loader.
basis: section:Each Class Loader Has Its Own Singleton, Enum Included

aspects.says: A constructor guard refuses a reflective call only if it reads a field that is already set when the call can happen: the static final instance (or a holder's field), not a lazily set field or a flag.
basis: section:A Private Constructor Stops new, and Nothing Else

aspects.says: The holder idiom makes creation lazy and thread-safe but by itself survives none of reflection, serialization or a second loader; a guard and readResolve must be added, and the enum refuses the first two without code.
basis: section:The Holder Idiom Chooses When the Instance Is Built; Only the Enum Refuses Copies

aspects.says: In a named module that doesn't open the singleton's package, setAccessible(true) from another module throws InaccessibleObjectException.
basis: section:A Private Constructor Stops new, and Nothing Else
aspects.reason: it needs two named modules on a module path, while the graded runner builds one class-path project; unit 2.2.1 checks the same refusal on JDK classes

aspects.says: Building the one instance in main and passing it through constructors keeps one instance in production and lets each test build its own.
basis: section:A Static Singleton Carries One Test's State Into the Next

aspects.says: A class is identified by its name and its defining loader, so two loaders that define the same singleton class hold two instances and two states, and casting one to the other's type fails.
basis: section:Each Class Loader Has Its Own Singleton, Enum Included

aspects.says: readResolve returning the instance makes readObject return the live singleton with its live state; what was written is discarded.
basis: section:Deserialization Makes a Second Instance Without Running the Constructor

aspects.says: setAccessible(true) lets any class-path code call a singleton's private constructor and get a second instance with fresh state.
basis: section:A Private Constructor Stops new, and Nothing Else

aspects.says: A singleton stays one per process only when one shared parent loader defines it; a child-first loader must send the shared API to the parent.
basis: section:Each Class Loader Has Its Own Singleton, Enum Included

aspects.says: Tests in one JVM share a static singleton, so one test's changes decide whether the next passes, and a reset hook fails once tests run in parallel.
basis: section:A Static Singleton Carries One Test's State Into the Next
